title: Parks and Recreation Master Plan approved
subtitle: Council also backed a guaranteed livable income letter, approved Culture Plan 2030, updated public art and grant policies, and announced budget town halls.
overview: Council approved the Parks and Recreation Master Plan {{vote:m9}}, with funding to be considered through future operating and capital budgets. A set of five playground accessibility amendments was referred to staff to work with the Accessibility Advisory Committee, and staff will report back if new service levels are needed {{vote:m8}}. Staff said the amendments could affect playground replacement budgets, so residents should expect further reports before any change to service levels.

Council directed the Mayor to write to federal and provincial leaders calling for a national guaranteed livable basic income {{vote:m12}}. A softer wording that would only encourage governments to explore the idea was defeated {{vote:m11}}. Council also approved Culture Plan 2030 with an added direction on displaying City-owned artifacts {{vote:m15}}.

On the consent report, Council dissolved the Community Grant Allocation Panel and moved grant decisions to staff, and directed a new emergency management by-law. It also approved a Public Art Policy update. The Mayor announced ward budget town halls in November, ahead of the budget release.

decisions.detail: Council approved the August 2023 plan and referred its funding needs to future operating and capital budgets.

Five proposed amendments on accessible play equipment and rubber-surface playgrounds were referred to staff to work with the Accessibility Advisory Committee and report back if new service levels are required.
Council directed the Mayor to write to federal and provincial leaders calling for collaboration on a national guaranteed livable basic income {{vote:m12}}.
Council approved the plan, referred its costs to the 2024-2027 multi-year budget, and asked staff to report by Q2 2025 on displaying City-owned artifacts.
Council approved the policy update, changed the Public Art Reserve Fund sources, and referred costs to the multi-year budget and a possible City Hall clock relocation to staff for 2027 celebrations.
The Community Grant Allocation Panel will be dissolved, grant authority goes to the Deputy CAO of Public Services, and equity-related policy changes were added.
Staff were directed to bring forward a new Emergency Management Response By-law replacing the 2019 by-law.

debate: Delegates on the master plan questioned why it took 14 years to bring forward and why it no longer includes a separate open space master plan, as some other cities have. Staff said related natural heritage and river system work is covered in other strategic documents.

Delegates and the Accessibility Advisory Committee chair said wood chip playground surfaces are not usable with wheelchairs, walkers or strollers, and described talk tubes as segregating. Staff said current playgrounds meet accessibility standards and that wood fibre has known challenges.

Several councillors worried the playground amendments had not been reviewed by the advisory committee or costed. Staff said they could affect capital budgets and the number of playgrounds replaced each year, and that approving the plan was needed to keep work moving. The mover said some of the amendments had little budget impact.

On guaranteed income, supporters cited poverty, housing pressure and pilot results. Some councillors preferred wording that only encouraged governments to explore the idea, citing unanswered implementation questions such as work incentives and inflation. Others said 'work collaboratively towards' already allows for exploration.
